A 31-year-old Black woman, a schoolteacher, has 2 months of dry cough, exertional dyspnea, fatigue, night sweats and painful red nodules on both shins. T 37.9 C, SpO2 95%, lungs clear. Serum Ca 10.9 mg/dL; 24-h urine Ca raised; ESR 48 mm/h.

A 38-year-old office manager who smokes 2 packs a day has 3 months of dry cough, exertional dyspnea and fatigue. Few crackles, SpO2 94%. FEV1/FVC 0.80, DLCO 58%. Chest film: fine nodular and web-like markings in the upper and middle zones with the bases spared.

A previously healthy 24-year-old man develops fever, cough and rapidly worsening dyspnea over 4 days; no transfusion, aspiration, travel, animal exposure or new drug. RR 34, SpO2 82% on room air, needs intubation. Chest film: diffuse bilateral opacities; viral PCR panel and blood cultures negative.
